Summary:
Quick discovery for Blue Ridge evaluating Redwood's self-serve hosted API. Main asks: how fast can they hit first token using quickstart/free credits, what limitations on free tiers, and when would Dedicated/Private be required. Security questions (SOC 2, SSO, VPC) came up; Redwood AE/SE explained typical PLG flow, invites for credits, and follow-up technical demo.

Topics covered:
- Onboarding path: sign-up, free credits, quickstart notebook, API key creation
- Time-to-first-token: typical <5 minutes demo expectations and gotchas (IP allowlist, network egress)
- Differences: Hosted (fast), Dedicated (committed throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC 2, SAML/SSO, KMS integration, retention policies
- Next steps for a small benchmark and SE deep-dive

Transcript:
[00:00] Claudia Morris: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Claudia, AE at Redwood Inference, and with me is Ethan from the SE team. How are you all?
[00:06] Nora Li: Good, thanks. Nora here. Excited to learn more — we got your invite.
[00:09] Tom Becker: Tom, CTO. We want to see how fast we can get something into prod, or at least into a POC.
[00:13] Claudia Morris: Totally. The goal here is we'll run through our PLG quickstart — how to get first token, what free credits look like, plus when people typically graduate to Dedicated or Private. Ethan, want to kick off with the simple flow?
[00:23] Ethan Gupta: Sure. So basic onboarding is signup, API key creation in the console, then a quick curl or SDK call. Most teams can see a token in under five minutes assuming no outbound network block. We'll also share a one-click notebook.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Quick question: "first token under five minutes" — does that assume anything about IP allowlists? Our infra blocks a lot of egress.
[00:42] Ethan Gupta: Good callout. If your environment blocks outbound traffic, you'll need to allow the Redwood endpoints or do the private deployment path. For hosted quickstarts, usually you need to open egress to api.redwood.ai (we sometimes see it transcribed as redwood dot interface, sorry) or use a jump host.
[00:55] Samir Khan: What's included in the free credits? We want to test a few embeddings flows and some chat completions.
[00:59] Claudia Morris: We typically provide a small bundle of credits aimed at getting you to first-token and some light evaluation — embeddings, short generation. For larger scale POCs we'd move to a dedicated trial. I'll include exact numbers in the follow-up email.
[01:10] Nora Li: Are there rate limits on the PLG keys? We don't want to accidentally hit throttling while testing.
[01:15] Ethan Gupta: PLG keys have conservative rate limiting by default to protect the shared backend. You can request a temporary raise for POC test windows. For production, Dedicated gives you guaranteed throughput.
[01:25] Tom Becker: Can you summarize when we'd pick Dedicated vs Private? Our compliance team will push for VPC if we store customer PII.
[01:31] Claudia Morris: Sure. Hosted is fastest to start — the PLG path. Dedicated when you need predictable capacity and committed SLAs plus isolation. Private (VPC or on-prem) when you need network controls, KMS/HSM integrations, or strict data residency.
[01:41] Priya Nair: On KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[01:44] Ethan Gupta: Currently hosted uses platform-managed keys, but we have options for private deployments to bring your KMS. We also offer envelope encryption options for some enterprise customers. We'll share our security pack.
[01:53] Nora Li: Cool. For the quickstart, is there an SDK or is it curl only?
[01:56] Ethan Gupta: Both. We have language SDKs and example curl. Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"Say hi"}' — that should return tokens. We'll include a ready-to-run snippet.
[02:12] Tom Becker: Any gotchas we've hit before that slow down time-to-first-token?
[02:16] Ethan Gupta: The main ones: corporate firewall/egress, strict SSO requiring SAML setup before generating keys, and in rare cases internal proxy cert validation. Also, spelling note — sometimes our domain gets misheard in notes, so watch for that.
[02:30] Samir Khan: How quickly can we get a demo that focuses on latency? We care about 95th percentile for short prompts under 200 tokens.
[02:36] Ethan Gupta: We can do an SE-led latency/throughput session where we run a small bench with your prompt profiles. Typically 30–60 minutes. We'll need a list of sample prompt lengths and expected QPS.
[02:46] Nora Li: For benching we'd probably start with 10 qps and then push to 100 qps. Cost is also a concern — can you give rough unit cost guidance for hosted?
[02:54] Claudia Morris: We'll provide high-level numbers in the follow-up. Our Optimize toolkit can also suggest batching/quantization moves once we see your workload. For early POC it's more about viability than perfect cost modeling.
[03:06] Tom Becker: Security docs — SOC 2/ISO and logs — are those included in the PLG docs?
[03:11] Claudia Morris: Yes, we'll attach our compliance pack (SOC 2 report, pen test summary, audit log capabilities). For deeper legal review we can coordinate with our security team.
[03:19] Priya Nair: If we did a quick hosted test and liked performance, what's the lead time to move to Dedicated?
[03:24] Claudia Morris: Usually a few weeks depending on region and GPU availability — Dedicated requires capacity planning. We'll surface estimated time when you tell us desired throughput.
[03:31] Samir Khan: Any public benchmarks?
[03:33] Ethan Gupta: We publish model profiles in the console — latency/cost baselines across instance types. For your specific prompts we prefer doing an on-customer bench.
[03:41] Nora Li: Great. For the first token test, what's the exact flow you want us to run?
[03:44] Ethan Gupta: Quick steps: 1) Sign up and confirm email, 2) In console create API key, 3) Run curl or SDK snippet (we'll send), 4) Capture the time from request start to first token response, 5) Send screenshot and any error logs to the thread. That'll help us troubleshoot if something blocks you.
[03:58] Tom Becker: If we hit network egress restrictions, could we do a temporary dedicated sandbox in our cloud?
[04:03] Claudia Morris: We can provision a pre-configured dedicated trial but it usually has a lead time and requires a commit. For purely testing, simpler to allow egress or use a jump host with NAT. We'll help with firewall endpoints.
[04:13] Priya Nair: Does Redwood's console show token-level cost in PLG?
[04:17] Ethan Gupta: Yep — token breakdown is visible. You'll see cost per request, latency, and model. That helps diagnose when prompts are expensive.
[04:24] Nora Li: Ok, security-wise also SSO/SAML — would that block quickstart if we didn't enable it?
[04:29] Claudia Morris: No — SSO is optional. You can create a local console account for the quickstart and then later migrate to SSO for team onboarding.
[04:36] Samir Khan: Any particular sample prompts you recommend for embeddings?
[04:39] Ethan Gupta: Keep them representative — a few short sentences and some longer docs. We'll share a small eval set.
[04:45] Nora Li: Who should I loop in for the SE demo? Our platform folks and maybe an infra person.
[04:50] Claudia Morris: Great — include Priya and maybe an infra lead. We'll send a Calendly for a 45-minute slot next week.
[04:56] Tom Becker: Ok sounds good. Can you also send a list of endpoints that need to be whitelisted?
[04:59] Ethan Gupta: Yes, we'll include a network whitelist in the follow-up (api.redwood.ai + associated IP ranges).
[05:05] Priya Nair: For the POC — what does success look like?
[05:08] Claudia Morris: We generally define success as: 1) you can call the hosted API and get tokens, 2) we run a small bench and meet your latency floor (e.g., 95p under X ms), and 3) you have a plan for data handling (retention, logs).
[05:19] Nora Li: Ok, next steps?
[05:21] Claudia Morris: I'll email the quickstart + credits info and the cURL/SDK snippets. Ethan will share the bench script. We'll set up the SE session for latency/throughput.
[05:29] Tom Becker: Sounds good — thanks all.
[05:31] Claudia Morris: Thanks — we'll follow up with the items.

(End of recording)
